explicit_validation.explanation: Paper explicitly validates LLM evaluator against human experts by comparing preferences on 50 dialogue pairs, reporting 78% agreement between GPT-4o evaluator and human majority preference

prompts.notes: Appendix A.3 provides configuration and general prompt template for evaluator agent but not the exact detailed prompts or scoring rubrics; describes three analytical perspectives (Holistic, Teacher-centric, Student-centric)

guidelines.notes: Appendix F.4 mentions evaluation materials and questionnaire design but full guidelines not provided; includes template for human rating (1-10 scale) and feedback form with general questions about pedagogical effectiveness

sample_size.notes: 50 dialogue pairs (each pair: one with learning gain vs one without) randomly selected from 148 Unique Improvement Count (UIC) cases; represents approximately 40% of performance gap between best and worst teachers

quantitative_scores.notes: 39 out of 50 cases where human expert majority preference aligned with GPT-4o evaluator's selection
Learning gain teachers received average rating of 7.38/10 vs control group 6.41/10

validation_results.summary_finding: GPT-4o evaluator shows 78% agreement with human experts on identifying effective teaching behaviors, with teachers producing learning gains receiving significantly higher human ratings (7.38 vs 6.41/10)

criteria_mapping.notes: LLM evaluator uses structured 17-dimensional scoring framework while humans provide overall ratings and preference judgments; validation focuses on binary preference alignment rather than dimensional scoring
